integration_notes: O/A (DEF-J-1, high; D-20/D-21 metering): the first divergence of a fresh-process rerun of a civilisation (balanced seed 41, day 1) is a hosted site's request billed cpu_ms 4.096 / cu 204.8 instead of the remembered 0.101 / 5.05: crucible.sandbox.metering bills a fresh measurement that exceeds MEMO_TOL x anchor + MEMO_SLACK_NS, so billing depends on machine load (in-process reruns and two disk-cache-off fresh processes were identical to the first run). Please resolve an exceedance deterministically (bill the anchor and flag the job, or re-measure until two measurements agree) so the same spec and seed give the same hashes on one machine.

SEM/D (DEF-J-1, high, latent): crucible.semantic.space computes missing representations in batches whose composition depends on the world's record AND on the process-wide/machine-wide RepCache (memory LRU + ~/.cache/crucible/space, shared by every process of every agent); padded batched encoding is not batch-invariant (CPU probe: 5 of 6 padded texts differ from their single encoding by 0.9e-7..7.2e-7, the unpadded one is bitwise equal). Request: make a representation a function of its bytes only (padding-free groups by exact token length, or one item per forward pass) and add a test of bitwise equality of batched vs single encoding on CPU and GPU; then free reruns of one spec and seed become exact and the civ free-rerun counters (SP-10.0 free_reruns_exact, Gate P free_resume_equal) can become criteria.

SEM/D: world state grows ~16 MB per simulated day in a development civilisation after the event window is full (live RSS 2.6 GB at day 31 -> 3.1 GB at day 61; 365-day runs reach ~8 GB live plus a verification child): most of it is likely the per-world space records (vec + chunks + features of every recorded item kept in state). Keeping recorded vectors as content-addressed array blobs referenced by events (like cols.batch) would bound long-run memory; Gate P suites are memory-bound on this machine.

KERNEL/A: crucible.civ.determinism.regenerate_continuation mirrors the loop of World.regenerate on a loaded world (it sets World._regen); a public kernel API World.regenerate_from(world, events) would remove that coupling. The observer diagnosis (8 sequential in-process runs of balanced seed 5: 4 distinct 3-day trajectories; inv/acc/fromblob/otherworld identical, pure/digest/replay/snap(day 3) different) shows no observer effect of World.replay/from_blob/another world: the divergence is intermittent inference numerics (DEF-J-1), not process-global state.

ECON: crucible.economy.work posts to the forum (_post, the ask-board request) as ids.pid(i) without ids.ensure_principal: 3 forum posts in a 6-day civilisation are authored by principals that do not exist (O.2 identity_consistency_violations). Please call ids.ensure_principal(ctx, i) before ctx.call(..., as_principal=p) (as population.web does).

ECON/INFRA (O.2 duplicate energy_price): in a civilisation the datacenter fleet (crucible.domains.infra_world, module fleet) prices electricity from its own per-site tariff while industry grids carry the regional energy price; when both are installed the fleet should read the price of the grid of its region (one fact). Likewise products vs industry retail listings, pop.employer vs industry own operators (industry's operators should be population members), forum boards vs community.communities (D-21 migration) and gov.constitutions vs inst.inst_charters are second copies holding facts in every civilisation (crucible.substrate.facts KNOWN_DUPLICATES).

ECON (crucible.economy.work, search ranking; finding of the SP-2.1b seed-54 probe at 5bcd1e5): individuals who look for a service search with their format's task text, and their own help threads ('Looking for a service: <task text>') and the replies to them carry exactly that text in the title, so they fill the results of the query (10 of 10 for pack.knapsack after three days); a provider's capability declaration or announcement is then never read unless someone names its host in one of those threads. Realistic as a crowding effect, but worth a look: forum replies inherit the thread title in the index ('Re: ...') and outrank the declaration that answers the query.
